Marathon Petroleum gained 1.5% today as oil refining indicators remained tight and geopolitical tensions around Iran continued to support energy prices. US crude is holding at $83.90 per barrel while refineries are running at 97.4% capacity—near maximum—which keeps margins healthy for refiners like MPC. The U.S. Navy blockade of Iran's oil exports, described as a shift to economic warfare after months of military strikes, removes barrels from global supply and supports the price floor that refiners depend on.

The stock has climbed 3.8% over two weeks as the conflict in the region has dragged on longer than initially expected, keeping geopolitical risk premiums baked into oil prices. With storage levels moderate (718 million barrels of oil, 206 million of gasoline), tight refining capacity, and no near-term resolution to the Iran situation, the structural conditions that favor refiner profitability remain in place.
